acceptance_criteria: Probe unavailable, timeout, protocol failure, malformed response, and valid inventory absence have distinct typed outcomes.
Required tool expectations are derived from one versioned runtime registration contract.
Tests prove probe failure never reports every expected tool as observed-missing inventory.
Valid inventories still report exact missing and present tool sets deterministically.
blast_radius: BOT ERRORS daily health, MCP socket and JSON-RPC probing, runtime tool registration, alert classification, operator diagnosis, and inventory regression tests.
evidence_summary: Three stable body-free live reads pinned the open identity, four current labels, timestamp, URL, and body hash while API and SSH main remained exact. Current tool_inventory returns the entire REQUIRED_TOOLS list as missing when the socket is absent or json_rpc tools/list throws, so transport and protocol failure is represented as valid inventory absence. The required list is independently sourced from BOT_ERRORS_REQUIRED_TOOLS defaults rather than a runtime-exported registration contract. A deterministic prior falsifier forced json_rpc failure and reproduced both the probe failure and the full missing-tool set. falsifier_or_remaining_gap: The finding would be falsified if probe unavailable, protocol failure, malformed response, and valid inventory absence produced distinct typed outcomes, and expected tools came from the same versioned runtime contract that registers them. Exact source collapses failures to REQUIRED_TOOLS missing and uses an independent environment default.
impact: Transport outages can page as tool-removal incidents, while an independently maintained expectation list can drift from the runtime and create false positives or false negatives.
